  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Diagrams of existing Mplus results}

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(MplusAutomation)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = requireNamespace("htmlwidgets", quietly = TRUE) &&
  requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE))
```

`mplus_diagram()` displays an existing Mplus analysis as an interactive HTML
widget. It reads a complete `.out` file or a single model returned by
`MplusAutomation::readModels()`. No Mplus installation is required to display
fixed results, and the function does not estimate a model.

Install the optional rendering packages once with
`install.packages(c("htmlwidgets", "jsonlite"))`. Install `shiny` as well to save
configuration directly from an interactive editor. Ordinary HTML output can be
viewed and edited offline.

## Read and display a model

```{r initial}
out <- system.file("extdata", "mplus-diagram", "cfa-ml.out", package = "MplusAutomation")
diagram <- mplus_diagram(out)
diagram
```

The graph retains original variable identities, fixed parameters and reported
estimates. Labels edited in the browser are display names. The default view
keeps the full model structure, uses STDYX when present, hides residual
variance decorations and known default covariances, and prints two decimals.
Explicit and unknown-origin covariances remain visible. Paths are not removed
because their p-values are large.

```{r model-object, eval=FALSE}
model <- MplusAutomation::readModels(out, quiet = TRUE)
mplus_diagram(model, options = list(
  scale = "unstandardized", digits = 3,
  parameter_labels = TRUE, default_covariances = TRUE
))

# A directory or model list always requires an explicit selection.
mplus_diagram("results", select = "my-analysis.out")
mplus_diagram(list(primary = model), select = "primary")
```

Only estimates actually printed in the selected results table are displayed.
If STDYX is absent, a visible diagnostic explains the switch to unstandardized
estimates. If only one STDYX parameter is absent, that coefficient remains
unavailable at the standardized scale; its raw value does not replace it.
Fixed structural values and standardized coefficients are separate. A loading
fixed to 1 in the original model can have a standardized value other than 1.

By default, coefficient labels use two decimal places, a mathematical minus
sign (U+2212), and no leading zero for standardized values below one in magnitude.
Raw coefficients retain their leading zero. Relationship labels sit on the path with a small white clearance around the
whole text box, protecting decimal points from crossing lines. Diagram text uses
Times New Roman with Times/Liberation Serif/serif fallbacks. Significance stars use the selected scale's reported p-value: `*` for
p < .05, `**` for p < .01, and `***` for p < .001. Paths with a valid p-value
at least .05 use dotted lines without coefficient labels by default, except original-scale fixed constraints. Missing or invalid p-values are not treated as
nonsignificance. On the original scale, fixed parameters remain solid without stars. A loading
fixed to 1 on the original scale may have a valid STDYX p-value: standardized
stars and dots follow that actual p-value, as requested. The original constraint
is available in the tooltip and Constraints panel, without a printed `[fixed]`
suffix. Set `stars = FALSE` or `nonsignificant_dotted = FALSE` in
`options` to disable either display feature. No path is removed by significance.
The **Dotted nonsignificant** checkbox cycles through checked (dotted without
labels, the default), mixed (dotted with labels), and unchecked (solid with
labels). Set `nonsignificant_hide_values = FALSE` with
`nonsignificant_dotted = TRUE` in `options` for the mixed state. The global
Values and Parameter labels settings still apply when path labels are enabled.

Factor covariances in CFA and vertically aligned exogenous-variable
covariances in SEM connect on the left. Ordinary variable correlations now use
the same cubic bow as CFA/residual correlations: the base proportion is 15% of
the endpoint distance. SEM automatic layouts enlarge a bend when measurement
indicators obstruct that side; the simplified view accounts for its own visible
nodes. This initial routing does not replace a deliberately saved bend.

Use **Path** in edit mode to select a relationship even when it is covered by
another path or node. **Line type** offers **Straight**, **Curve**, and
**Polyline** for relationships other than variance arrows. Ordinary single-headed
paths default to straight; existing saved bends and default covariance curves
remain curves. Drag the curve handle to change its bend. A polyline has two
right-angle corners: drag its handle or, after selection, its middle segment to
move the routing lane above/below or left/right of the endpoints. Its coefficient
starts at the middle of that segment and can be dragged separately. Changing line
type recenters the coefficient; moving nodes preserves the stored bend/routing
offset. Routing is manual and does not automatically avoid every other node.
Line types and offsets are saved separately for full and simplified views and
support undo/redo and SVG/PNG export. Variance arrows keep their rotation controls.

Select a correlation and drag its existing curve handle to adjust the bend.
For curved correlations, drag an arrowhead to switch both connections together, preserving the bend:
left/right for vertical pairs, top/bottom for horizontal pairs. There are no
additional visible endpoint handles. If arrowheads overlap, select the intended
line first. The connection side is saved separately from curvature, supports
undo/redo and is independent in each view. When residual arrows are visible,
switching their correlation side rotates the corresponding residual arrows and
values together; the correlation remains attached to their tails.

Turning on **Residuals** shows short arrows instead of loops, with values just beyond their outer tails;
residual covariances connect to the corresponding residual-arrow tails. Turning
Residuals off reconnects those covariances directly to the variables. Exogenous
factor covariances still connect to the factors, and RI within-person components
retain their statistical identities. Missing significance display options are automatically
filled in when an older version-1 configuration is loaded.

## Longitudinal structure

The supported continuous, single-group, single-level ML/MLR corpus includes
CFA, observed path models, SEM, mediation, CLPM, RI-CLPM with explicit within
factors or supported `^` residual syntax, and linear growth. Growth time scores
include fixed zero loadings. RI within components remain model nodes even when
residual decorations are hidden.

Model syntax establishes structural roles. Variable names alone do not prove
wave or construct membership. Supply a mapping when the intended longitudinal
layout is not established by the syntax:

```{r longitudinal}
panel <- system.file("extdata", "mplus-diagram", "clpm-ml.out", package = "MplusAutomation")
mplus_diagram(panel, mapping = list(
  family = "clpm",
  waves = c(X1 = 1, X2 = 2, X3 = 3, Y1 = 1, Y2 = 2, Y3 = 3),
  constructs = c(X1 = "X", X2 = "X", X3 = "X",
                 Y1 = "Y", Y2 = "Y", Y3 = "Y")
))
```

Mappings supplement the source model; contradictory roles and unknown
identifiers are rejected. Unsupported syntax that changes the model cannot be
silently dropped to produce a partial graph. Multigroup, multilevel, mixture,
categorical, Bayes, latent interaction and nonlinear/piecewise growth models
are outside this release's intended scope.

## Edit, save and reuse

In an ordinary widget, click **Edit diagram** to adjust the current display.
Select one or more nodes (Shift-click for multiple selection), or a path, then
click **Remove object**. Removing a node also removes its incident paths,
residual arrows and their labels from both views. **Undo** reverses the change;
**Restore automatic layout** restores removed objects in both views and resets
the current view's layout. Removals are saved with the configuration and affect
SVG/PNG exports without changing the underlying Mplus results.
Drag nodes, use Shift to select multiple nodes, align selections, select a
path to adjust its curve, and drag its label to improve spacing. For a residual
arrow, drag its shaft, control point or value around the variable: the arrow
rotates through 360 degrees at a fixed length, always aims at the variable center
with its head on the boundary, and keeps its value
beyond the outer tail. Visible residual correlations follow that tail. Display names
can include Chinese text. Undo/redo and restoring the automatic layout affect
presentation only. The full and simplified views retain their own positions.

Temporary widget edits do not write to the R project. To save directly from
an interactive R session, use the local editor and an explicit configuration
target:

```{r editing, eval=FALSE}
# Requires the optional shiny package and an interactive R session.
# Choose an existing project directory for the destination.
saved <- mplus_diagram(out, action = "edit",
                       config = "my-analysis.diagram.json")
saved
```

**Save and return** validates and writes the configuration before ending the
editor. **Cancel and return** keeps the prior saved configuration. An error
while saving leaves the editor available for correction. The editor runs on
loopback; ordinary widgets and report rendering do not start that service.
RStudio's Viewer is used when available, with a browser alternative.

```{r reuse, eval=FALSE}
mplus_diagram(out, config = "my-analysis.diagram.json")
```

With a reliable `.out` source, the default configuration filename is the same
stem with `.diagram.json`. A model object without a reliable source path needs
an explicit save target. A relative filename stored inside an R model object
does not establish its original directory after a working-directory change.
Pass the `.out` filename directly, read the object with
`MplusAutomation::readModels(normalizePath(out))`, or supply `config` explicitly.
Reading a diagram never writes a configuration.

Configuration stores positions, curves, display names, visibility and options.
It also records the source title, output basename, estimator, Mplus version and
an SHA256 identifier for the imported output/results snapshot. This content ID
is not a Mplus run UUID. Older configurations without source metadata still load;
exports refresh metadata from the current results. Source metadata does not
choose a save destination or replace results. Re-estimating the same structure keeps compatible
presentation state while refreshing estimates. A different structure, invalid
configuration or unknown configuration version produces a diagnostic and an
automatic layout; the original configuration file remains intact.

Option priority is: explicit `options`, compatible saved state, explicit
project `defaults`, then package defaults. For example, `options = list(digits
= 3)` overrides saved precision; `defaults = list(digits = 3)` does not.

## Reports, offline HTML and image export

Place `mplus_diagram()` in an ordinary R Markdown HTML chunk. Rendering reads
compatible saved configuration or uses a deterministic default. A
noninteractive call with `action = "edit"` fails immediately with guidance,
instead of waiting for a person.

```{r html-export, eval=FALSE}
htmlwidgets::saveWidget(diagram, "model.html", selfcontained = TRUE)
```

Self-contained output embeds the diagram data, scripts and styles. A reader
can edit the diagram without R or a network connection. Each diagram in a
report has separate controls, selection and undo history. Refreshing the HTML
restores the embedded starting state.

**Export config** downloads presentation state. **Import config** applies a
compatible file to the current widget. These downloads do not overwrite your
project or the HTML file. To use a downloaded configuration in the next R
report, place it at the chosen configuration path and pass it through `config`.

The **SVG** and **PNG** controls export the current graph, including display
names, paths and labels, without the editing toolbar. PNG provides a scale
selector. Browser limits can prevent very large bitmap exports; the interface
reports such failures. SVG remains a vector format. The canvas and image exports omit the model title
and explanatory legend. PNG multipliers scale both pixel dimensions: 2× has
twice the width and height, hence four times as many pixels as 1×.

## Diagnostics and verification limits

Mplus warnings remain visible. A normal termination message does not erase an
improper-solution warning, and a graph is not a substitute for reviewing the
analysis. Failed estimation and insufficient results are rejected. A supplied
model object must retain enough source syntax to determine topology and
constraints reliably.

The repository includes fixed engine outputs and independently transcribed
relationship expectations. CI consumes them without running the commercial
engine. A separate developer workflow checks installed package resources and
renders a two-diagram, self-contained report in a fresh R process while
verifying that its saved configuration is unchanged. Those checks do not
constitute human approval of visual quality or certification of every
RStudio/browser/operating-system combination. The project tracks that
acceptance separately.
